original_question: Construct a continuous theory for particles with positive and negative mass, or equivalently for billiards in pseudo-Euclidean metrics, and determine whether the resulting Euler-like equations for a fluid of negative density exhibit interesting phenomena.
target_in_paper: Boris Khesin, item 3: "Is there a fluid of negative density?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact Boris Khesin open problem about constructing a continuous version of the positive/negative-mass particle theory, links it to pseudo-Euclidean billiards, and preserves the paper’s second question about whether the corresponding Euler-like equations for a fluid of negative density show interesting phenomena.
missing_details: The paper anchors the problem to a specific discrete model: three point-like beads with masses m1, m2, m3 on a frictionless ring undergoing elastic collisions.
The nearby context specifies the reduced billiard model obtained by using momentum and energy conservation and quotienting out rotational symmetry.
The triangle data are explicit: tan(alpha1) = sqrt(m1(m1 + m2 + m3)/(m2 m3)), together with the cyclic permutations for alpha2 and alpha3.
The negative-mass regime is not arbitrary; the paper imposes the condition (m1 + m2 + m3)m1m2m3 > 0.
The acute/obtuse distinction is part of the intended scope: if all masses have the same sign, the associated triangle is acute; otherwise it is obtuse.

The pseudo-Euclidean description is presented in the paper as an alternative fixed-triangle viewpoint with an appropriately rescaled Euclidean metric that becomes pseudo-Euclidean when negative masses are present; the draft states this more strongly as an outright equivalence.

The paper’s question is exploratory rather than classificatory: it asks to construct a continuous version of this specific theory and to investigate whether interesting phenomena occur for the associated Euler-like equations, not to prove a complete theorem or classification.
A nearby limiting case is mentioned: if one mass, say m3, tends to infinity, the model reduces to billiards in a right triangle, equivalently two beads constrained to a segment between two walls.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, or phrases such as "for all sufficiently large m" occur in this problem; those categories are inapplicable here.
refined_question: Construct a continuous version of the one-dimensional elastic-collision theory of point particles with positive and negative masses that is motivated by the three-bead-on-a-ring model: for masses m1, m2, m3 on a frictionless ring, after reduction by rotational symmetry the dynamics is equivalent to billiards in a triangle with tan(alpha1) = sqrt(m1(m1 + m2 + m3)/(m2 m3)) and cyclic permutations, and allowing negative masses subject to (m1 + m2 + m3)m1m2m3 > 0 yields the obtuse-triangle regime. In the corresponding fixed-triangle viewpoint, where negative masses lead to a pseudo-Euclidean metric, formulate the associated Euler-like equations for a "fluid of negative density" and investigate whether they exhibit interesting phenomena.
justification: The draft is aimed at Boris Khesin’s third problem, whose title and content match it almost verbatim: the paper asks for a continuous version of the positive/negative-mass particle theory, explicitly mentions the relation with pseudo-Euclidean metrics, and then asks whether the corresponding Euler-like equations for a "fluid of negative density" display interesting phenomena. The missing stand-alone details all come from the immediately preceding motivation on the same pages: the three-bead model on a frictionless ring, the reduction to triangular billiards, the explicit angle formula, and the admissibility condition (m1 + m2 + m3)m1m2m3 > 0 for allowing negative masses. This is therefore not related to Conjecture 1 or Problems 1–3 in the later Albach–Hryniewicz–Oancea section.
